sections.title: The Analogy: Learning from Mistakes
sections.content: Introduce the neural network as a 'decision-making machine.' Use the concept of a 'Teacher-Student' feedback loop where the network makes a guess, receives a grade, and adjusts its internal 'knobs' (weights) to improve.
sections.example: A student trying to identify photos of cats vs. dogs: if they guess 'cat' but it's a 'dog,' the internal frustration acts as the error signal.

sections.title: Visualizing the Network Architecture
sections.content: Explain the layer structure: Input (raw data), Hidden (feature extraction), and Output (final decision). Use a graphical representation of nodes connected by variable-strength wires (weights).
sections.example: Nodes as lightbulbs; the brightness of the light represents the activation strength, and the thickness of the connecting wire represents the 'weight' of the connection.

sections.title: Defining the Loss Function (The Yardstick)
sections.content: Introduce the concept of 'Loss' as the numerical distance between the network's prediction and the truth. Visualize this as a valley in a hilly landscape where the goal is to reach the lowest point (the minimum error).
sections.example: An archer shooting at a target: the distance from the bullseye is the 'Loss.' The further away, the higher the correction needed.

sections.title: Backpropagation: The Credit Assignment Problem
sections.content: Explain the backward pass: Error signals travel from the output layer back to the input. We calculate how much each weight contributed to the error using partial derivatives (visualized as gradient arrows indicating which way to turn the 'knobs').
sections.example: A chain of dominoes falling: if the final domino doesn't fall, we trace backward to see which specific domino in the line was knocked out of alignment.

sections.title: Gradient Descent: Refining the Model
sections.content: The final step: updating the weights in the direction that reduces the error. Emphasize that small steps (learning rate) prevent overshooting the goal.
sections.example: A hiker descending a mountain in thick fog: they can't see the bottom, so they feel the slope under their feet and take a small, careful step downhill in the direction of the steepest descent.
